result_text:
`all_files.zip` now looks up and names its entries from the configured aspect names, so renaming `buildAndDeployment` no longer breaks the export. The change is in `reports/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/reports/dataexporters/DataExporter.java`, in the zip section of the export method.

- **What changed:** The hard-coded five-entry literal is replaced by a loop over the five scope aspects (main, test, generated, build and deployment, other). Each entry is named with `DataExportUtils.getAspectFileListFileName(aspect, "")`, which is the same helper that writes the loose `aspect_<name>.txt` files, and read from the same text folder. The order is unchanged.
- **Why it fixes the collateral loss:** The old code read `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt`, which no longer exists after the rename. The `FileNotFoundException` was swallowed by the enclosing `catch (Throwable)`, so `all_files.zip` and `git-history.zip` (which sits in the same try block) were never written. Now the read succeeds and both zips are written.
- **Default config:** Entries stay `aspect_main.txt`, `aspect_test.txt`, `aspect_generated.txt`, `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt`, `aspect_other.txt`, in that order.

Verification: the reports module compiles offline and its test suite passes (`ReportFileExporterTest`, 1 test). I did not add a test for `DataExporter` and did not run an export against a renamed config, so the rename case is verified by reading the code, not by a run. Nothing is committed.
